chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majluwayh narrated to me, he said: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me, he said: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi narrated to me from al-Fadl ibn Salih al-Asadi from Muhammad ibn Marwan from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever hates us, the Ahl al-Bayt, Allah (Exalted and Mighty) will resurrect him as a Jew.' It was asked: 'O Messenger of Allah, even if he testified the two declarations of faith?' He said: 'Yes, they will only be veiled by these two words at the shedding of his blood, or when he pays the Jizyah while being humiliated.'

Then he said: 'Whoever hates us, the Ahl al-Bayt, Allah will resurrect him as a Jew.' It was asked: 'How so, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'If he lives in the time of the Dajjal, he will believe in him.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَیْتِ: Ahl al-Bayt (the Family of the Prophet)

ai.seo_question: Why does hatred of the Ahl al-Bayt result in being resurrected as a Jew according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to emphasize that hatred of the Ahl al-Bayt corrupts the essence of faith, rendering even the two testimonies (Shahadatayn) superficial. The Prophet clarifies that such individuals are resurrected as Jews not necessarily by ethnic conversion, but by adopting their historical stance of rejecting divine leadership, a trait that culminates in their acceptance of the Dajjal. This highlights the Shia theological link between love for the Prophet's family and true belief, contrasting it with the rejection seen in previous nations.
